actions.name: create_task_from_calendar_event
actions.description:
Create a task from a calendar event. Creates a new task based on a calendar event, linking all related events
(sharing the same iCalUID) to the task and removing the event from
unavailable time planning calculations. Related events already linked to a
task or time log keep that link; returns 409 when the event itself is.

A recurring master event becomes one repeating task mirroring its RRULE, starting on
the first occurrence on or after `date` (default today). Exception rows, subtasks and
unsupported rules are rejected; `estimatedMinutes` defaults to the event duration.

Request (application/json): payloadcalendarevent.TaskFromEventRequest

actions.name: get_companies
actions.description:
Get all companies. Retrieve all companies for the provided filters.


On this endpoint you can filter by custom fields. The syntax for the
query parameter is the following:

    customField[id][op]=value

Where:
  - [id] is the custom field ID
  - [op] is the operator to apply when filtering, different operators are
    allowed according to the custom field type
  - [value] is the value to apply when filtering

For example, if I want to filter a dropdown custom field with ID 10 to only
return entries that have the value "Option1" we would do the following:

    customField[10][eq]=Option1

The allowed operators are:
  - like
  - not-like
  - eq
  - not
  - lt
  - gt
  - any

actions.name: create_multiple_records
actions.description:
Create multiple records. Create multiple custom item records in a single call. Referenced section names
are created-or-used and assignee emails are resolved to users server-side, so an
importer working from a file need not resolve either per row. A caller that
already holds section ids may send "sectionId" instead, which takes precedence
over "sectionName".

By default the batch is transactional: the first bad row aborts the request
with a 4xx identifying the row under "meta.index", and nothing is created.
Set "options.partialSuccess" to true to create rows independently instead:
valid rows are created and failures are reported per row under "failed" by
request index. When nothing could b...

options.description: BulkOptions are the batch-wide options of a bulk create.

partialSuccess.description:
PartialSuccess: true creates the valid rows and reports failures per row
under "failed"; false (the default) aborts the batch on the first bad
row, creating nothing.

items.description:
BulkRecord is a single record within a BulkRequest. Sections may be referenced by
name (created-or-used server-side) and person fields by email (resolved
server-side), so an importer need not resolve them per row.

A caller that already holds section ids may send SectionID instead, as the
single-record endpoint takes: it wins over SectionName, and is validated against
the custom item like any other, so a section belonging to another item is still
refused. Accepting both spares a caller having to know which of the two spellings
this endpoint wanted.

actions.description:
Get the current user's personal tasks. Returns the personal tasks for the logged-in user.


On this endpoint you can filter by custom fields. The syntax for the
query parameter is the following:

    customField[id][op]=value

Where:
  - [id] is the custom field ID
  - [op] is the operator to apply when filtering, different operators are
    allowed according to the custom field type
  - [value] is the value to apply when filtering

For example, if I want to filter a dropdown custom field with ID 10 to only
return entries that have the value "Option1" we would do the following:

    customField[10][eq]=Option1

The allowed operators are:
  - like
  - not-like
  - eq
  - not
  - lt
  - gt
...

actions.name: persist_accepted_previewed_schedule
actions.description:
Persist an accepted, previewed schedule. Writes the supplied plan verbatim without calling the solver, so it can never
return 502. The requested project must exist and the caller must be allowed to
modify its schedule (403). The plan is re-authorized against the caller's
projects and their members before any write: a task that is unknown, deleted
or outside the requested projects, or an assignee who is not a project member,
returns 403. Tasks are resolved regardless of task or tasklist privacy, as on
/persist; write permission on the project is what is required. The plan is
rejected as 422 if invalid: bad, inverted or out-of-range dates, capacity
cells that do not match a scheduled task's...

basedOnRunKey.description:
BasedOnRunKey is the runKey of the /preview response the plan came from.
Optional. It is stored with the applied plan so its preview's inputs and
validation can be looked up. At most 256 characters after trimming, with
no commas.

plan.description:
ApplyPlan is the plan /apply writes. It accepts the /preview body unchanged:
planId and runKey are accepted and ignored, because /apply writes the plan it
is given; send the runKey as basedOnRunKey.

runKey.description: RunKey is ignored; send it as basedOnRunKey.

status.description:
Status is only populated by the scheduler's solver-failure envelope
(INFEASIBLE / MODEL_INVALID / UNKNOWN). A normal solve omits it.
The client uses it for the defensive 502 guard; 05/06 ignore it.

items.description: AutoScheduleRespTask is one entry in AutoScheduleResponse.Tasks.
AutoScheduleRespUser is one entry in AutoScheduleResponse.Users.
AutoScheduleRespUserDate is one day entry in AutoScheduleRespUser.Dates.
an object (see the provider's API docs)

projectIds.description:

include.description:
include

`users` lists the assigned people as relationships. `users.levels` adds
to each of those relationships a `meta.level` holding the level that
person holds for the skill, which is what the skills matrix renders its
cells from; a person assigned but not yet rated carries `meta.level`
null. `peopleCount` reports how many people hold each skill, which costs
a query of its own and so is opt-in.

assignedToUserIds.description: filter skills by users assigned to it

actions.name: create_new_skill
actions.description: Create a new skill. Creates a new skill global to the entire installation.

skill.description:
Skill is the body of a skill create. An update sends a different body, which
does not accept `people`.

people.description:
People is the per-person form of UserIDs, carrying a level each. It is
an alternative to UserIDs and a request carrying both is rejected.

items.description:
PersonLevel names one person together with the level they hold for the
skill, so a single request can carry several people at a different level
each.

level.description:
Level is the ordinal rating to store: an explicit null clears it,
leaving the skill assigned but unrated, and omitting it altogether
leaves whatever is already stored alone.

user.description: Relationship describes the relation between the main entity and a sideload type.

actions.name: delete_many_skills_at_once
actions.description: Delete many skills at once. Bulk delete a number of skills.

actions.name: assign_skill
actions.description:
Assign a skill. Replaces the set of skills a single user holds. The body names them either as
plain ids in `skillIds` or, to carry a level for each, as `skills`; a body
naming both is rejected. Skills the user holds and the body does not name are
removed.

skillIds.description:
SkillIDs names the skills as plain ids, without a level each. It is an
alternative to Skills and a request carrying both is rejected, so it is
not required; on the replace-set path an absent list is meaningful in
its own right, and unassigns every skill.

skills.description:
Skills is the per-skill form of SkillIDs: the same set of skills, each
carrying the level the person is to hold for it. It is an alternative to
SkillIDs and a request naming both is rejected; an absent list means the
skills are taken from SkillIDs instead.

items.description:
SkillLevel names one skill together with the level its holder has for it, so
a single request can carry several skills at a different level each.

level.description:
Level is the ordinal rating to store: an explicit null clears it,
leaving the skill assigned but unrated, and omitting it altogether
leaves whatever is already stored alone.

skill.description: Relationship describes the relation between the main entity and a sideload type.

actions.name: delete_existing_skill
actions.description:
Delete an existing skill. Removes a skill. It's still possible to recover the skill.
Marks all related skill assignments as deleted.

actions.name: update_existing_skill
actions.description:
Update an existing skill.

Only the name is honoured. Skill assignments and the levels people hold are
set through the people endpoints, not here, so this body has no `people`
field and one that names it is rejected.

skill.description:
SkillUpdate is the set of skill fields an update honours: the name.

Assignments are not changed here. Who holds a skill, and at what level, is
set through the people endpoints - PUT and POST /skills/{id}/people for a

is rejected: there would be nothing to do.

actions.name: list_tasks
actions.description:
Get all tasks. Return multiple tasks according to the provided filter.


On this endpoint you can filter by custom fields. The syntax for the
query parameter is the following:

    customField[id][op]=value

Where:
  - [id] is the custom field ID
  - [op] is the operator to apply when filtering, different operators are
    allowed according to the custom field type
  - [value] is the value to apply when filtering

For example, if I want to filter a dropdown custom field with ID 10 to only
return entries that have the value "Option1" we would do the following:

    customField[10][eq]=Option1

The allowed operators are:
  - like
  - not-like
  - eq
  - not
  - lt
  - gt
  - any

actions.name: total_count_of_completed_tasks
actions.description:
Total count of completed tasks. Returns the total number of completed tasks. Only the tasks that the
logged-in user can access will be counted.

actions.name: get_total_count_of_late_tasks
actions.description:
Get total count of late tasks. Returns the number of late tasks. Only the tasks that the logged-in user has
access to will be counted.

actions.name: returns_preview_list_of_recurring_dates
actions.description:
Returns a preview list of recurring dates. Exactly one mode must be used: either taskId (uses the task's existing repeat
settings) or dueDate + frequency (and optional selectedDays, duration, endsAt,
monthlyRepeatType). Combining taskId with dueDate or frequency is an error.

On an installation that skips weekends the selectedDays frequency drops
weekend occurrences instead of moving them to a weekday, so a selection made
up entirely of Saturday and Sunday can never repeat. That returns a 400
carrying meta.code "skipWeekendsExcludesAllSelectedDays" rather than an empty
list. A selection that mixes weekend and weekday days is previewed with only
the weekdays that survive.

selectedDays.description: comma separated list of sequence weekdays (1=Sunday .. 7=Saturday) the task repeats on

monthlyRepeatType.description: how the monthly repeat type should be interpreted

frequency.description: repeat frequency to use when previewing without an existing task

endsAt.description:
date after which the sequence stops repeating; must be after dueDate and
cannot be more than 10 years after dueDate

dueDate.description: due date to use when previewing without an existing task

cursor.description: pagination cursor returned by a previous request

taskId.description:
preview an existing task's saved repeat settings; cannot be combined with
dueDate or frequency

limit.description: number of dates to return per page

duration.description:
number of days between repeats; must be 1 or greater. Only used by the
everyXDays and everyXDaysWeekday frequencies, ignored by the others.

actions.name: get_subtasks_for_specific_task
actions.description:
Get all subtasks for a specific task. Return multiple subtasks according to the provided filter.


On this endpoint you can filter by custom fields. The syntax for the
query parameter is the following:

    customField[id][op]=value

Where:
  - [id] is the custom field ID
  - [op] is the operator to apply when filtering, different operators are
    allowed according to the custom field type
  - [value] is the value to apply when filtering

For example, if I want to filter a dropdown custom field with ID 10 to only
return entries that have the value "Option1" we would do the following:

    customField[10][eq]=Option1

The allowed operators are:
  - like
  - not-like
  - eq
  - not
  - lt
...

actions.name: copy_project

Copy a project. Creates a duplicate of an existing project. This endpoint allows you to specify a new name and description for the cloned project and choose which elements (tasks, milestones, files, etc.) should be carried over from the source project.

To clone a project you need the ability to create projects (userCanAddProjects) or be a site admin.

Note that cloning large projects with many elements may take some time to process. The response will be returned once the cloning process is complete.

cloneProjectName.description: The name for the new cloned project. If not provided the new project will have the same name as the original project with an incremental number suffix.

cloneProjectAction.description: The action to perform when cloning a project.

description.description: Description of the new project. When not provided it will use the description of the original project.

companyId.description: Company/Client ID that the new project will be related to. By default it will use the same company/client as the original project.

copyFiles.description: The files from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyMessages.description: The messages from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyMilestones.description: The milestones from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyTasks.description: The tasks from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyTasklists.description: The task lists from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyNotebooks.description: The notebooks from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyLinks.description: The links from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyComments.description: The comments from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyFollowers.description: The followers from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyInvoices.description: The invoices from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyTimelogs.description: The time logs from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyExpenses.description: The expenses from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyWebhooks.description: The webhooks from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyProjectRoles.description: The project roles from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyCustomFields.description: The custom fields from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyCustomItems.description: The custom items from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyProjectUpdates.description: The project updates from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyRisks.description: The risks from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyForms.description: The forms from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyAutomations.description: The automations from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyPeople.description: The people from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyProjectPrivacy.description: The project privacy settings from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyBudgets.description: The budgets from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyAllocations.description: The allocations from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyLogo.description: The logo from the original project will be copied to the new project.

copyProjectPrefs.description: The project preferences from the original project will be copied to the new project.

newFromTemplate.description: Whether the project should be created from a template. If true, the daysOffset parameter can be used to set the start and end dates of the new project based on the date provided in the date parameter.

toTemplate.description: Whether the new project should be converted to a template.

templateDateTarget.description: Specifies whether targetDate represents the project's start or end date. Accepted values: 'start' (default) or 'end'. When 'end', the start date is calculated by subtracting the template project's duration from targetDate. Only applicable when newFromTemplate=true.

targetDate.description: The desired start or end date for the cloned project (determined by templateDateTarget). Used only when creating a project from a template (newFromTemplate=true). Accepted format: YYYYMMDD. Defaults to the current user date if omitted.

daysOffset.description: The number of days to shift all scheduled dates in the cloned project relative to the base date. When cloning from a template, it defines the project duration span. When copying an existing project, it shifts the original start and end dates by this many days. If omitted, calculated automatically from the source project's date range.

A page contains 100 entries, but you can increase the page size to a maxium of 500 entries by using 'pageSize' parameter. To select a different page of data, set the 'page' query parameter to a value greater than zero. The total number of time entries in the project is in the X-Records HTTP header. X-Pages will be set to the total number of pages, and X-Page will be set to the current page.

Additional Notes:

The date field returned in the response is in UTC date/time The toDate, toTime, fromDate and fromTime are specified in your timezone. ---

fromdate.description: string (YYYYMMDD) - The start date to retrieve from

sortorder.description: asc or desc - The order to sort the returned data

userId.description: Return time logs for a specific user only

billableType.description: string (billable or nonbillable).Filter the Time Entries to those that are Billable or Not Billable.

invoicedType.description: string (invoiced or noninvoiced) - filter the time entries to those that have been Invoiced or not.

projectType.description: string (all, active, archived) - Filter the time entries to those in Active projects, Archived projects or All projects.

showDeleted.description: string (true or false) - Filter time entries to include deleted time sheet entries or not

tagIds.description: numeric - Include one or more Tag IDs here to return only the time entries with those tags attached (eg &tagIds=23,445,454)

updatedAfterDate.description: string YYYYMMDDHHMMSS

page.description:

actions.description:

With this call, the parameters seachFor and searchTerm are required. Your path will look like this:

/search.json?searchFor={resource}&searchTerm={search_term}

**Eg. Seaching using tags:**

To search for a resource with an attached tag of 'My Test', do the following:
To search for a Tag, you use a hash symbol and square brackets in the searchTerm, like this : #[My Test]
Then where performing a query to the API, you need to ASCII encode the # [ ] symbols, so a GET query to the API will look like this:

GET to /search.json?searchFor=messages&searchTerm=%23%5BMy+Test%5D

In the above example, #, [ and ] have been changed to %23,...

actions.name: list_current_user_s_data_views
actions.description: List the current user's data views. Returns a paginated list of data views (saved filters) belonging to the authenticated user, optionally scoped to a project, data type, or updated-since timestamp.

projectId.description: Restrict results to data views belonging to this project.

title.description: Filter data views by exact title match (SQL equality, not a partial/substring match).

useCaching.description: Whether to use the server-side response cache (ETag caching).

showDeleted.description: Include soft-deleted data views in the results.

getEmoji.description: Parse emoji shortcodes in title/description to unicode.

pageSize.description: Number of records per page.

dataType.description: Restrict results to data views of this type (e.g. tasks, projects, milestones). Pass "ALL" to return every type, or a comma-separated list of types.

getShareData.description: Include sharedWith (users/companies/teams) information for each data view. This also changes which records are returned: when true, the result set additionally includes data views that other users have shared with you (via user, company, or team shares), not just your own views.

updatedAfterDate.description: Only return data views updated after this timestamp. Must be in YYYYMMDDHHMMSS format.

dataViewId.description: Return only the data view(s) with this ID. Accepts a comma-separated list of IDs. When set to a value other than 0, this replaces userId, projectId, dataType, title, isTemporary and includeTemporary as the record filter (those parameters are ignored); showDeleted and isDefault still apply.

fulldata.description: Accepted by the endpoint but currently has no effect on the request or response.

sortBy.description: Field to sort results by. Any other value is treated the same as "name".

sortOrder.description: Sort direction. The endpoint accepts any value; anything other than "asc" or "desc" (case-insensitive) is silently treated as "desc".

userId.description: Return data views belonging to this user (defaults to the current session user).

isDefault.description: Only return data views marked as the user's default/selected view.

actions.name: create_new_data_view
actions.description: Create a new data view. Creates a new data view (saved filter) for the current user, or for another user when acting as an owner-company admin.

userId.description: Defaults to the current session user.

isProjectSpecific.description: If provided, must match whether projectId is greater than 0.

get.description: Comma-separated list of related data to include in the response (e.g. "dataView").
